title: Prevalence of minimum dietary diversity, by population group (children aged 6 to 23 months and women aged 15 to 49 years)
graph_title: Prevalence of minimum dietary diversity, by population group (children aged 6 to 23 months and women aged 15 to 49 years)
national_indicator_available: Prevalence of minimum dietary diversity, by population group (children aged 6 to 23 months and women aged 15 to 49 years)
national_indicator_description: Diverse diets, which are essential for providing the micronutrients needed for healthy growth and development, reducing the risk of deficiencies.
computation_definitions: Minimum Dietary Diversity (MDD) for children aged 6-23 months measures the proportion of children consuming foods from at least five out of eight standard food groups within a 24-hour period. Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) measures the proportion of women consuming at least five out of ten standard food groups within a 24-hour period.
computation_calculations: (Number of children or women eating 5 or more food groups) / (Total number of children or women in sample) * 100
other_info: Please see the linked data source for more detail, including alternative measures of dietary sufficiency and analysis of regional inequalities.
comments_limitations: While the global metadata specifies that the MDD-W indicator should be provided for non-pregnant women, these figures do not differentiate women based on pregnancy status. For more information about methodological limitations, please see the linked data source.
indicator_name: Prevalence of minimum dietary diversity, by population group (children aged 6 to 23 months and non-pregnant women aged 15 to 49 years)
target_name: By 2030, end all forms of malnutrition, including achieving, by 2025, the internationally agreed targets on stunting and wasting in children under 5 years of age, and address the nutritional needs of adolescent girls, pregnant and lactating women and older persons
indicator_definition: Minimum Dietary Diversity (MDD) for children aged 6-23 months measures the percentage of children 6–23 months of age who consumed foods and beverages from at least five out of eight defined food groups during the previous day. Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) measures the percentage of non-pregnant women aged 15-49 years who consumed foods or beverages from at least five out of ten defined food groups during the preceding 24 hours. These are population-level food group-based indicators that capture dietary diversity, a key characteristic of healthy diets.
